blocks.text: sermon. After duly praising Allaah, he said, "Take note that you people should not make your dowries exorbitant. If the news ever reaches me that any of you has paid more that what Rasulullaah ﷺ paid or what was paid to him (as dowry for his daughters), I shall deposit the excess into the public treasury."

After Hadhrat Umar (RA) had alighted from the pulpit, a woman from the Quraysh objected. "O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" she said, "Is the Book of Allaah more worthy of following or your words?" "The Book of Allaah of course," Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "what do you mean by this?" She explained, "You just forbade the people from paying dowries in excess of four hundred Dirhams whereas Allaah says in His Book:

blocks.arabic_text: وَآتَيْتُمْ إِحْدَاهُنَّ قِنْطَارًا فَلَا تَأْخُذُوا مِنْهُ شَيْئًا
blocks.text: '...when you have given one of them (your wives) a fortune (as dowry) then do not take anything from it...'" [^1]

Hadhrat Umar (RA) twice or thrice repeated, "Everyone has more understanding than Umar." He then returned to the pulpit and said, "O people! I had forbidden you from paying dowries in excess of four hundred Dirhams (the prohibition no longer stands). A man is at liberty to give whatever he pleases from his wealth." [^2]
Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "Had (exorbitant) dowries been a source of status and elevation in the Aakhirah, the daughters and wives of Rasulullaah ﷺ would have been most deserving of it." [^3]
The Practices of Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA) in the Matter of Dowry
Hadhrat Ibn Seereen reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) allowed dowries of two thousand Dirhams while Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) allowed dowries of four thousand. [^4]

Hadhrat Naafi reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) married Hadhrat Safiyya (RA) for a dowry of four hundred Dirhams. She however returned it saying that it was insufficient. He then added another two hundred Dirhams without Hadhrat Umar (RA) knowing about it. [^5]
Hadhrat Ibn Seereen narrates that when Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA) married a woman, he sent a hundred slave women to her, each one of them carrying a thousand Dirhams. [^6]
